statement: There is exactly one smooth complex plane quintic through twenty general points. It has geometric genus six.

source.version: arXiv:0906.3828v4 (18 January 2010), primary PDF reinspected 4 November 2026

scope: Irreducible plane curves of degree five and geometric genus six through twenty general complex points.
notes:
Figure 1 has N_(5,6)=1. Equivalently, the projective space of quintic forms has dimension twenty, so twenty independent point conditions determine a unique form up to scale, smooth for general points.

The numerical count is associated with the earlier recursion (Caporaso–Harris for plane curves of arbitrary genus). Fomin–Mikhalkin’s table remains the inspected verification source; their floor-diagram Theorem 1.6 explicitly restates Brugallé–Mikhalkin. This is not a claim that the individual numerical value was historically first found by the cited recursion.
